data.description:
# `_resolve_target`'s "already provider-qualified" test is `":" in model`, and real Bedrock ids contain a colon

## Impact, stated first

**Any model class configured with `provider = "bedrock"` and a CANONICAL versioned Bedrock model id
is broken, and it fails with an error that names the wrong thing.** Canonical Bedrock ids carry a
version suffix containing a colon — `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`,
`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` — which is the majority form of the ids AWS publishes.
Only the unversioned aliases (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`)
happen to work. This is in the middle of what epic 061c ships ("first-class AWS Bedrock provider").

## Mechanism, confirmed by experiment (no LLM spend)

`model_classes._resolve_target` decides whether to prefix the configured provider by asking whether
the model string already contains a colon:

    def _resolve_target(model: str, provider: str | None) -> str:
        # Already provider-qualified -- return as-is, never double-prefix.
        if ":" in model:
            return model
        resolved_provider = provider or infer_provider(model)
        return f"{resolved_provider}:{model}" if resolved_provider else model

A versioned Bedrock id satisfies `":" in model` for the WRONG reason — the colon is inside its
version suffix, not a provider separator — so the function returns the bare model and the
operator's explicit `provider = "bedrock"` is silently discarded:

    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",              "bedrock")
      -> "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"                      # correct
    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", "bedrock")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"                 # provider LOST
    _resolve_target("anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0",     "bedrock")
      -> "anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0"                     # provider LOST

Downstream that unqualified string is read back as `provider:model` on the FIRST colon, so:

    infer_provider("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1"

…and the provider factory rejects it. Reproduced end-to-end through the real class table:

    parse_class_slots({"standard": {"model": "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
                                    "provider": "bedrock"}})
    resolve_class("standard", slots) -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"

## Observed live (this is how it was found)

A real `rebar review-code` run with `standard` pointed at the versioned Bedrock haiku id produced:

    verdict: INDETERMINATE, llm_ran: False
    llm_error: "step 'verify' failed: unknown provider
                'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1';
                registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']"

The whole gate degraded to INDETERMINATE. Note how misleading the message is: the operator
configured `provider = "bedrock"` — which IS registered — and the error blames a "provider" that is
actually most of their model id.

## Why the current test cannot simply be tightened to "split on the last colon"

The two forms are genuinely ambiguous on a naive scan: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains TWO
colons, and `us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains one. Splitting on the first colon mis-reads the second
form; splitting on the last mis-reads the first. The distinguishing fact is not colon position but
whether the prefix names a REGISTERED PROVIDER — the same set the error message already prints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a configured `provider` is honoured for a model id containing a colon: a class configured
      `{model: "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", provider: "bedrock"}` resolves to
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
- [ ] an ALREADY-qualified string is still not double-prefixed: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` stays
      unchanged (this is the property the current test was protecting and it must not regress)
- [ ] the qualified/unqualified decision is made against the registered provider set rather than by
      the presence of a colon, so a future provider name needs no second edit here
- [ ] a bare id with no configured provider still infers as it does today (back-compat: every
      existing unversioned value resolves byte-for-byte unchanged)
- [ ] tests cover BOTH Bedrock id shapes — unversioned alias and canonical `...-v1:0` — because
      the unversioned form passes today and hid this bug
- [ ] `infer_provider` agrees with the qualifier on every shape the tests cover (they are two halves
      of one contract; a fix to one that leaves the other splitting differently is not a fix)
- [ ] the failure mode is checked at a level an operator sees: a misconfigured provider must not
      surface as "unknown provider '<most of my model id>'"

## Notes

Found while gathering ticket 3768's non-default-provider evidence, which the bug BLOCKS for any
versioned id; that evidence was obtained with unversioned aliases as a workaround. Not folded into
b690 (whose change is already `LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1`) because it is an unrelated seam with
its own back-compat surface. Filed under epic 061c per the operator's standing ruling that provider-
seam wiring is epic work; the epic's mandate is to ship without bugs, so flagging rather than
deferring silently.
data.title: Bedrock: a configured provider is silently DROPPED for any model id containing a colon (the canonical '...-v1:0' form)
